structure.title: Part I · Anna visits a house in disorder
structure.text: Anna comes to Moscow to persuade her sister-in-law Dolly to forgive an unfaithful husband. In the same household Levin hopes to ask Kitty to marry him. The early gatherings let the same remark or dance matter differently to several people who can all see one another.

structure.title: Parts II–III · Two households imagined
structure.text: Anna and Vronsky discover how far desire can unsettle a settled life. Levin returns to his estate and tries to imagine what a household might be worth building. Mowing a field, attending a race and receiving a caller become occasions on which private hopes meet quite public expectations.

structure.title: Parts IV–VII · The work of living together
structure.text: Setting up a home brings expenses, servants, illness and questions about children. Tolstoy moves between fashionable rooms and country houses where practical arrangements can carry the entire weight of a marriage. Who may make a visit, and whose invitation counts, become urgent questions for Anna.

structure.title: Part VIII · The final movement changes the scale
structure.text: Levin worries about what it means to live well even when a day's work and the people he loves seem to give him a ready answer. Public arguments over duty to strangers press up against the intimate demands that have filled the novel.

people.name: Anna and Karenin
people.text: Anna is unusually quick to sense what somebody else is feeling. Karenin has spent a career conducting difficult business through correct procedures. In a marriage each talent can leave an entire part of the other person's life untouched.

people.name: Vronsky
people.text: Admiration comes easily to a man with money, charm and excellent horses. Loving Anna asks him to recognise obligations for which his regiment's code of honour offers little guidance. His freedom to circulate in society can conceal how differently that society treats her.

people.name: Levin and Kitty
people.role: A landowner and a young woman entering society
people.text: Levin's schemes for improving agriculture meet resistance from people who know the work differently. Kitty learns to care for people at times when the supposedly more experienced Levin can scarcely bear to enter the room. The two kinds of practical knowledge rarely enjoy equal prestige.

context.title: Scandal has an uneven geography
context.text: What a man can acknowledge among his comrades may cost a woman access to a drawing room or her own child. Attending an opera, accepting a dinner invitation and taking a seat in a carriage all bring private relationships within reach of an audience.

notice.text: Follow a look past its first interpreter.
notice.why: At the ball Kitty studies Anna's face for evidence that she is loved. Anna's pleasure, the observer's fear and Vronsky's behaviour all enter the same scene. Seeing something accurately does not give anyone possession of the whole encounter.

notice.text: Observe the hands doing unfamiliar work.
notice.why: A gentleman with a scythe and a frightened visitor at a sickbed both discover forms of competence that argument cannot confer. The people beside them have acquired their ease through repetition and necessity.

opening: Anna arrives to help repair her brother's marriage after his affair. She knows how to soothe an injured wife and make a difficult household breathe again. Then she meets Vronsky, and the understanding she brings to other people's lives offers little protection in her own. Tolstoy follows desire into train stations, nurseries, drawing rooms, and the anxious intervals between meetings, making an attachment feel like an entire world while showing all the people and obligations that continue to exist beyond it.
